Required for app, website, supported in-app, and usage-limit protection: lets Switchly detect foreground changes and the visible information needed for configured rules.
Required for screen-time statistics and daily app limits. Enable “App usage data” access for Switchly.
Some devices do not offer an “Unrestricted” battery option. If you already enabled the highest available background setting for Switchly, that may already be the maximum supported on your device.
If exact alarms are not allowed, time-based schedules may be delayed or not run at the correct time.
Set Switchly to Unrestricted/Not optimized. Android “Optimized” mode can still delay schedules, geofences, receivers, and background reliability.
Needed so time-based schedules can run reliably at the correct time.

Required for opening Switchly from NFC tags. Make sure system NFC is enabled and, when available, allow Switchly under Special app access → Launch via NFC. Android normally requires the device to be unlocked before scanning.

Required for Wi-Fi and location schedules. Wi-Fi triggers need location access to read the network name. Location schedules need precise location and “Allow all the time” for reliable background geofences.
Needed for Bluetooth-based schedules on Android 12+. You can enable it here before creating a schedule.
Required so Switchly can show status updates and reminders in the notification shade.
Required to hide notifications from apps blocked by your active profile (notification listener access).
To hide blocked-app notifications, enable notification access for Switchly.
Some devices add sleep, battery, auto-start, or background activity controls beyond standard Android. Review the guide for your manufacturer so Switchly is not restricted.
Lets Switchly detect foreground apps, supported browser URLs/text, and supported in-app navigation when needed to enforce configured protection and usage limits.

Switchly uses the Android Accessibility Service for app, website, and supported in-app protection.
What Switchly can access while the service is active: • The currently opened app and window changes • Visible text and URLs in supported browsers when needed to check website rules • In-app navigation events in supported apps when needed for in-app rules and limits
How Switchly uses this access: • To detect protected apps, websites, and supported in-app sections and redirect you away from them • To enforce app and website limits and record local usage/blocking statistics • To keep protection responsive when the foreground app or visible page changes
Accessibility is not used to prevent uninstall, enable Device Admin or Device Owner, or change managed-device policies. Those protections use separate Android device-management APIs and require separate user or provisioning steps.
Switchly does not use Accessibility to read passwords or private messages and does not sell or share Accessibility data for advertising. Processing for these protection features happens on your device.
You can decline this permission, but app, website, and supported in-app protection that depends on foreground detection will not work without it.
I understand what Accessibility lets Switchly access and how it is used for protection.

Android treats the Wi-Fi name (SSID) as location-related information. Switchly needs precise location to read the current Wi-Fi reliably. On some devices running Android 13 and newer, Nearby Wi-Fi devices may also be required.
Location permission denied. Wi-Fi schedules may not work without this permission.

Location schedules use geofences. For that, Switchly needs precise location. You can grant it here before creating the schedule. If the schedule should still trigger while the app is not open, background location is also required on Android 10 and newer.
Location permission denied. Location schedules may not work without this permission.

To run location schedules in the background, open Switchly’s app settings and change Location access to “Allow all the time”. On Android 11 and newer, this is granted from the system settings screen, not the first permission popup.
To detect connected Bluetooth devices for Bluetooth schedules, Android requires the “Nearby devices” permission. You can grant it here before creating the schedule.
Bluetooth permission denied. Bluetooth schedules may not work without this permission.
